subject: blind man cane
title: A Totally Blind Man Walked Through an Obstacle Course Untouched

scenes.text: A totally blind man walked through an obstacle course untouched.
Two strokes had destroyed the vision centers on both sides of his brain. His eyes worked. He saw nothing.
In 2008, scientists took his cane and filled a hallway with boxes, bins and a tripod.
He stepped around every one and never touched a thing.
He had no idea he'd done it. He hadn't seen a single object.
It's called blindsight. Older parts of the brain still get signals from the eyes. They just never tell you.

description:
A totally blind man walked the length of a cluttered hallway without touching anything.
The patient, a doctor known only as TN, lost his sight after two strokes damaged the visual cortex on both sides of his brain; his eyes are healthy, but he is completely blind and gets around with a cane. In 2008, a team led by Beatrice de Gelder set out boxes, bins and tripods along a corridor and asked him to walk it without his cane. He stepped around every obstacle and never collided with one, yet was not aware of having seen anything. The ability is called blindsight: more primitive parts of the brain still do some visual processing without the person knowing.
What do you think your brain does without telling you? Comment below.
first_comment: TN was surprised that the scientists were surprised. Asked if he could see, he said: No, I'm blind. What does your brain do without telling you?
